overview.description: Pegs and Jokers is a highly social, strategic board-and-card hybrid game, often described as 'Pachisi on steroids'. Players or teams race to move their pegs around a physical board (often made of interlocking wooden segments) using cards instead of dice. The game is famous for its 'Mean' mechanics, particularly the Joker, which allows a player to swap positions with an opponent, potentially undoing dozens of moves in a single turn. It is a staple of RV communities and family gathering 'Game Nights'.
overview.deck: Multiple 52-card decks (1 deck per 2 players) + Jokers

history.origins: Derived from the ancient Indian game Pachisi and the American game 'Sorry!'. It evolved into its current 'Pegs' format in the mid-20th century.
timeline: 1950s: First homemade 'Jokers and Pegs' boards appear in the US Midwest.
1980s: Modular board designs (interlocking pieces) make the game portable for RV travel.
2000s: Standardized rulesets emerge online, clarifying 'Split-7' and 'Backward-8' movement.
Present: Sold commercially by various boutique woodworkers and game companies.
history.evolution: The card-driven mechanic replaced dice to give players more agency and remove 'pure luck' from the race.
history.cultural: Commonly known as 'The Meanest Game' because of the positional swaps and the ability to send teammates forward while bumping enemies back.

setup.deck: 2 or 3 decks including all Jokers. Each player gets 5 cards.
setup.dealing: Five cards per player from one or more decks with Jokers; remainder forms the draw pile.

rules.objective: Move all 5 project pegs into your 'Safe' zone before the other team.
rules.gameplay: Partnership race for 4, 6 or 8 players. Five cards each; turn: draw one from stock, play one card to move pegs (or discard without moving if no legal move and draw replacement). Face cards and Ace move a peg out of start or 10 spaces; number cards move that many spaces; 7 splits between two pegs; 8 moves backward 8; Joker swaps your peg with any other peg on the track. First team to get all pegs home wins.
keyRules: Five cards dealt; draw one then play one (or discard without moving if no move possible). Must play a card that moves a peg if you have one; Joker is never forced. Pegs move clockwise; land on opponent sends them to start; land on partner sends them to in-spot. First team with all pegs in home wins.

strategy.basic: Always use your 'Come Out' cards (Face cards) as soon as you have an empty spot on the track. If you have an 8, use it to immediately back up into your Safe zone entryâ€”this skips nearly the entire board.
strategy.intermediate: TheSplit-7 Strategy: Use the 7 to 'Snipe' two different opponents or to move one peg into a safe spot while positioning another one for a bump on your next turn. The 7 is the most flexible tactical card in the deck.
strategy.advanced: Joker Sabotage: Do not use your Joker to save yourself! Use it to move your partner to the very end of the board, or to swap an opponent who is 1 space away from their Safe zone back to the beginning. Timing a Joker when your partner is in 'Trouble' is the mark of a pro team.
tips: If you can't move, you must discard a card and draw to 5. Avoid this by always keeping a 'Come Out' card and a 'Number' card in your hand.
Don't build 'Clumps'. If you have two pegs close together, an opponent's 7 can easily bump both of them.

list.name: Arizona Rules
list.description: Play card then move then draw (5 cards in hand). May move any team peg. 9 can split forward/backward. Joker from start must replace an opponent peg on track if team has pegs in start.

list.name: North Carolina Rules
list.description: Also called Jokers and Pegs; home is castle. 2 exchanges two pegs on main track. 7 and 9 must be split when possible. 10 must split between two different-colored pegs. Counting rule: after three turns unable to move, come out free with any card.

list.name: Pegoo
list.description: Florida variant; 20 holes per side. Joker moves peg to door (in-spot) or sends opponent to start. 2 moves 2 or exchanges two pegs on ring. Third-turn unable-to-move allows come out with any card.

difficulty.easy: Doesn't understand backward movement; never splits 7s; uses Jokers randomly.
difficulty.medium: Uses 8s for shortcuts; protects own pegs; basic team support.
difficulty.hard: Expert at 'Joker Positional Advantage'; perfectly calculates 7-splits; coordinates perfectly with its partner.

play_card.description: Play one card from hand to move a peg or pegs: face cards and Ace move out of start or 10 spaces; number cards move that many; 7 splits between two pegs; 8 moves backward 8; Joker swaps your peg with any other peg on the main track. If you have any non-Joker that allows a move you must play it; Joker is never forced.
play_card.constraints: Legal only when you have a card that enables a peg move, or you may discard without moving if no such card.

draw.description: Draw one card from the face-down stock at start of turn (basic) or at end of turn after playing (Arizona); keeps hand at five or six cards depending on variant.
draw.constraints: One draw per turn from stock.

discard.description: When you have no card (other than Joker) that allows any peg move, discard one card of your choice and draw a replacement; ends turn without moving. Played cards go face up to a discard pile.
discard.constraints: Allowed only when no non-Joker in hand enables a legal peg move.

edgeCases.text: Backing into home track is not allowed; pegs in home cannot move backward.
You may not land on or pass over your own peg; you may pass over or land on others' pegs.
Land on opponent: peg returns to start; land on partner: peg moves to in-spot if that in-spot is empty.
When all five of your pegs are home you move your left-hand partner's pegs (or next partner with playable pegs).
Joker cannot be played to an empty hole; only to a hole occupied by another peg.

engine.deckDescription: One or more standard 52-card decks plus Jokers; each player gets five cards. Pegs and Jokers Hybrid combines card play with peg movement on a board; Jokers act as wilds or have special movement.
engine.suitDescription: The four French suits (hearts, diamonds, clubs, spades) and Jokers. Cards drive peg movement; suit and rank determine how many spaces or which peg moves; Jokers have special effects.
engine.rankDescription: Standard ranks Ace through King; rank typically sets movement distance or peg selection. Jokers are wild or have fixed movement; the exact rules depend on the hybrid variant being played.
engine.dealPattern: Five cards each; remainder forms face-down stock.
